subject: Appendix: archival custody & retrieval SLA — clarification and redlines
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@nimbusfin.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Park <chris.park@nimbusfin.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 12:12:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on archival custody & retrieval SLA in Appendix A

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the DPA draft. Our legal team reviewed Appendix A (archival custody + retrieval SLA) and had a few clarifying questions before we circulate redlines internally. Two main items: 1) backup location and cross-border restore — we need clarity on whether on-demand restores for customer data could result in data crossing out of the EU (specific concern: emergency restores to US region for DR); and 2) retrieval SLA measurement and credits — the section currently says "retrieval within 48 hours" but doesn't define measurement start (request vs acknowledgement) or remedies if SLA is missed.

Quick asks: can you confirm whether standard backup restores ever cross geographies, and provide suggested language we can treat as a starting point for a carveout/exception process? Also, if you can provide a redlined Appendix A with an explanatory note for the retrieval SLA measurement point that would help speed review.

Appreciate it — we want to keep the commercial DPA moving while keeping our regulator happy.

Best,
Sophie Lane
Head of Legal Ops
Nimbus Financial

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on archival custody & retrieval SLA in Appendix A

Sophie —

Thanks for the clear note. Attaching a first-pass redline of Appendix A (file: Redwood_DPA_AppendixA_redline_v1.docx). High-level summary below, then the doc has exact text you can copy into your track changes: 

1) Backup location and cross-border restores
   - Short answer: standard automated snapshots and cold backups for EU customers are pinned to EU zones. On-demand restore to a non-EU region is not part of our default playbook.
   - Exception flow: we propose an explicit, auditable exception process where the customer requests a cross-border restore for disaster recovery or legal necessity. That request must be authorized by an authorized contact (customer security officer or legal) and will require documented justification. Restores triggered under exception are logged and subject to an approval SLA (we suggest 8 hours for approval).

2) Retrieval SLA measurement and remedies
   - We clarified measurement start: the SLA clock starts on Redwood's documented receipt of a valid retrieval request ("request received" timestamp). We also added a requirement for Redwood to acknowledge within 4 hours and to provide a target completion window thereafter (e.g., restore complete within 48 hours of receipt for standard archival retrieval).
   - Remedies: rather than an automatic credit on first breach we propose an escalation and remediation plan for the first missed SLA, with credits applying to repeated or root-cause identified systemic failures. The redline includes a cap and a process for dispute resolution.

3) Evidence and audit trail
   - We added language committing to provide an operations manifest for each retrieval that includes timestamps, region of restore, and list of objects restored. This will be available under the same evidence retention policy as audit logs (detailed in Appendix B).

If these options look acceptable to Nimbus legal we can incorporate the language into the formal DPA redline. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk through.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on archival custody & retrieval SLA in Appendix A

Hi Sophie — quick technical follow-up from our infra side (Hannah and I both looped Karthik for the restore details):

- Operational reality: For EU-region tenants we maintain primary snapshots and cold archives in eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 (customer-configurable). We do replicate a small set of operational metadata to a control-plane in us-west-2 for monitoring and telemetry (this does not include customer content).

- Restore mechanics: Standard restore operations will rebuild customer objects in the pinned EU region. The exception process Hannah suggested is used only in DR scenarios where a customer requests or authorizes a cross-region rebuild. The rebuild itself can be executed by our runbook operators or via an automated job; in both cases we will record the target region and provide manifest evidence.

- Suggested redline tweak for clarity: add the phrase "customer-authorized cross-border restore" and require a signed authorization template (we can provide a short form) to avoid ambiguity in audit.

Laura Bennett
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Questions on archival custody & retrieval SLA in Appendix A

Hannah / Laura —

Thanks, that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups after internal review: 

1) Our regulator will want an explicit statement that customer content will not be restored to or processed in a non-EU region unless the customer has provided a documented, time-stamped authorization. Your proposed "customer-authorized cross-border restore" language addresses this, but can you include the exact authorization template text in the redline? If you can add a short template (one paragraph that will be appended to the DPA) that would be ideal.

2) Backup snapshot retention overlap: we noticed the redline allows short-term replication for durability — can you confirm the maximum replication window for metadata copies (you mentioned control-plane telemetry)? We need a numerical upper bound for the DPA (e.g., metadata replication not to exceed 30 days unless otherwise agreed).

3) Attachment: I've added an annotated list of questions back to the doc (Nimbus_DPA_annotated_questions.pdf). Please confirm you received it.

If you can return an updated Appendix A with the authorization template and the metadata replication bound, we can push this through legal review next week. Happy to do a short 30-minute call on Monday with Karthik if needed.

Best,
Sophie Lane
Head of Legal Ops
Nimbus Financial
